description: Why: node_id is part of the HLC timestamp and determines uniqueness of concurrent HLC ticks across nodes. If node_id is regenerated on every restart (instead of persisted with the HLC checkpoint), two restarts of the same instance may produce the same HLC timestamps as a different instance with the same node_id, violating HLC uniqueness. What: hlc_persist.rs load_hlc_checkpoint loads wall_ms and logical from the database but not node_id. The caller then calls HlcClock::new_seeded which re-derives node_id from instance_id, so the persisted HLC value does not include node_id. Persist node_id alongside wall_ms and logical in the checkpoint table.
title: hlc_persist does not persist node_id; overwrites on reload
